name: The Thresher's Vale
summary: The bread-basket vale of the Crownlands: long, open, and golden half the year, watered by a Weavers' River side-arm. The first tribe's hearth — the First Kindling — was lit here in the First Stillness and has never gone out; Solmere was founded on its south bank, within sight of it.

geography.character: open grain-vale, threshing-floors, windbreak elms, shrine-hearths at crossroads

notable_sites.name: The First Kindling
notable_sites.note: The hearth of the first tribe, tended by rotation among the vale's farmholds. It has been lit since the divine covenant; letting it die is the one crime with no statute, because none was ever needed.

lore_notes: Solmere City rose on the vale's south bank in the Age of Ashes — licensed hedge-craft, taxed and inspected — until the Backfiring silenced it. The vale's folk still do not farm the south bank.
Tax day across most realms falls in Goldharvest; the vale's grain sets the price everyone else resents.
adventure_hooks: The First Kindling gutters for the first time in living memory; the keepers send for outsiders because whoever relights it must have no enemies.
A silent bell rings on the south bank where nothing stands anymore.
